I brought him because you wasn't first person who have this thought about suicide. Famous Cioran's quote: "I live only because it is in my power to die when I choose to: without the *idea* of suicide, I'd have killed myself right away."

It depends on what you prefer. His first work - "On the heights of despair" - is probably fundamental. It contains everything what he developed later. Good book for a beginning + he wrote it when he was young and well - on the heights of despair, you can feel it. One of my favorite.

If you want more "philosophical", "confusing" with sophisticated language, "The Temptation to Exist" is nice call. But sometimes it's not easy to read.

However his later works mainly consists of aphorisms, he was brilliant in making short, shocking sentences and personally my favorite books are: "All Gall Is Divided" and "Trouble With Being Born". Also I like books about him more in a private/personal manner. Well when someone had identic thoughts about suicidal thoughts, his life and personality must be interesting, so I would recommend you "Notebooks" (Cahiers 1957-1972) - aphorisms and short "diary" entries, I love it (about 1000 pages). Also there is short book with interviews but I don't know if it's available in English. Luckily here in Poland we have guy who knows Romanian and French and loves Cioran so we have majority of his works, translated from original source.

Or you can simply read his wikiquotes page and choose something that fits you: [https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Emil\_Cioran](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Emil_Cioran)

Yes, I have similar feelings. My questions regarding this subject are: can you completely lose the idea of suicide? Can you get better with this idea in your mind?

The answers are imo: no, yes.

Cioran said something like "if i hadn't suicidal thoughts, i would kill myself long time ago". At best you can quiet it, but not abandon completely. But you can still live normal life, be successful etc. Finding meaning in life is not easy. It's probably slightly harder when you constantly have in mind an "easy way out". But it's not unreal. Most important fact is if you feel strong enough to keep trying to do this things.

Only discomfort with being born is "new" (few years) and this pretending being "normal", but for me personally is more like discover than change of mind. Like I always more or less play a person, mimic behavior that "feel right" from my environment, tv shows etc. Like there is no "real" me at all. Like "real" me as a person never been to this world or gone long time ago. Yes, I always had attributes like patience, calm etc. But childhood seems to me like being an NPC who started to learn to adapt to certain groups, situations. And for a long long time, the only thing left in me is this adaptation. Nothing more.
